source.title: Occurrence, size distribution and polymer composition of microplastic particles in sediment cores from three lowland rivers
source.abstract: Riverbed sediment is thought to act as a long-term sink for microplastic particles, but vertical distribution data are scarce. We collected 36 sediment cores to a depth of 40 cm from three lowland rivers in central Europe during low-flow conditions in summer 2025. Particles between 20 micrometres and 5 millimetres were extracted by density separation and identified by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. Concentrations ranged from 42 to 310 particles per kilogram of dry sediment, with the highest values 300 to 800 metres downstream of wastewater treatment plant outfalls. Polyethylene and polypropylene together accounted for 68% of identified particles. Concentrations in the 20 to 40 cm layer were on average 2.6 times lower than in the top 10 cm, consistent with increasing plastic input over recent decades. We did not sample the water column, and we did not assess ecological or human health effects. Fibres shorter than 20 micrometres were below the detection limit of the method used.
source.tldr: Microplastic concentrations in riverbed sediment ranged from 42 to 310 particles per kilogram and were highest just downstream of wastewater treatment plants.
